# Motion coverage — current state

**Last verified**: 2026-09-13, after the Isharah DTW generation batch. Generated by `tools/motion_library_builder/builder.py rebuild-manifest`. Re-run the same command any time to refresh — it never downgrades an already-`ready` entry, and it enforces (raises, refuses to save) if the total ever stops being exactly 1,347 or if a duplicate token or mojibake label is produced. See `docs/MOTION_CONTRACT.md` for how a real motion file, like `stack.motion.json` alongside `stack_07.motion.json`, attaches to one canonical token instead of creating a second one.

| Dataset | Canonical tokens | ready | source_unavailable |
|---|---|---|---|
| jordanian_it | 165 | **165** | 0 |
| karsl | 502 | **502** | 0 |
| isharah | 680 | **674** | 6 |
| **Total** | **1,347** | **1,341** | **6** |

`165 + 502 + 680 = 1,347`, verified — see `backend/tests/test_manifest_correctness.py` (40 tests, runs on every test pass). **1,341 of 1,347 canonical tokens (99.6%) are `ready` with a real, schema-valid `signbridge-motion-v1` motion file** — this is physical recognition-dataset motion coverage, a separate number from semantic-planner coverage (see the bottom of this file and `docs/SEMANTIC_BRIDGE.md`).

The six intentionally-accepted-unavailable Isharah glosses (no confirmed local source, and no additional archives were downloaded to fill the gap): اليوم، بحرهو، رجوع، سيجاره، طاوله، وفاه.

`stack.motion.json` (the non-preferred earlier take) is recorded in `STACK`'s own `quality_metadata.alternate_takes_not_selected`, not as a second token — confirmed zero orphan motion files and zero duplicate tokens in every dataset.

## Generation history

### Jordanian IT + KArSL batch (2026-09-13, 17:57:27–18:34:33, 37m 6s)

158 remaining jordanian_it + 501 remaining karsl tokens generated (2 — ARRAY and karsl 0001 — had already been generated as approved samples in an earlier phase). **Zero failures across 659 tokens.** 357.24 MB written (173.37 MB jordanian_it + 183.87 MB karsl); disk free dropped 91.43 GB → 91.01 GB. Both datasets reached 100% ready.

**Bug found and fixed during post-batch verification**: `app/motions/manifest.py::_resolve_safe_path` built the generated-motion candidate path as `settings.motion_library / motion_file`, omitting the per-dataset subfolder (`.../<dataset>/<token>.motion.json`) the builder actually writes to. Every one of the 6 baseline motions (served from a different, correct path) worked and masked this; every one of the 659 newly generated motions would have 404'd through the real API despite the manifest correctly saying `ready` — caught by a live spot-check (`GET /api/motions/jordanian_it/POINTER` → 404) after the test suite had already gone green, because the test suite's own file-existence check used a separately-written helper instead of calling the production resolver. Fixed (added the missing `entry.dataset` path segment) and two regression tests added that call the *actual* `MotionManifest.resolve_file()`/the *actual* FastAPI app for a non-baseline token, so this class of gap can't recur silently.

### Isharah batch (2026-09-13, using per-sample DTW alignment — see `docs/ISHARAH_ALIGNMENT_INVESTIGATION.md` for the full method and resolution of the original alignment blocker)

Three representative samples validated first (beginning/middle/end of the continuous-sequence pool): `00_0355`/ا, `00_0682`/ابن, `00_0965`/ابتسامه. Production run then processed all 508 remaining source samples (672 remaining tokens; 2 of the 674-eligible tokens came from the 3 validation samples) — **zero generation failures**, final Isharah status `ready=674, source_unavailable=6`. Log: `tools/motion_library_builder/batch_isharah.log`. Per-sample alignment reports (509 files, DTW cost/overlay-error/quality-gate result for every sample): `debug/isharah_batch_alignment_reports/`.

## The Isharah alignment blocker: resolved

The earlier blocker (documented in full, and preserved, in `docs/ISHARAH_ALIGNMENT_INVESTIGATION.md`) was that `clips.csv`'s frame bounds index the pose-pickle-derived training feature sequence, while the locally downloaded `frames/00/*.jpg` images come from an independently-extracted, unrelated archive — with no metadata tying the two together and a non-constant frame-count offset between them, ruling out a naive proportional fix.

**Resolution**: rather than trying to map the stored 2-D pose array's frame indices directly onto the JPGs (which was never reliable) or using the 2-D pose array as motion data (which lacks the z/world-space geometry the frozen retargeter requires), `tools/motion_library_builder/diagnose_isharah_alignment.py` and `generate_isharah_motion_library.py` extract **fresh, full MediaPipe landmarks (with proper x/y/z and world-space coordinates) directly from the JPGs**, and use Dynamic Time Warping between that freshly-extracted timeline and the stored 2-D pose timeline **only to find which JPG frame range corresponds to a given gloss** — with a reversed-sequence control check and a calibrated-overlay-error quality gate per sample (a sample that fails the gate is marked `incompatible_source`, not `ready`). The motion data actually written comes entirely from the fresh, geometrically-complete MediaPipe extraction, never from the 2-D-only stored array. See `docs/ISHARAH_ALIGNMENT_INVESTIGATION.md` for the full dated resolution section, the validation evidence, and exactly how this avoids fabricating any missing coordinate.

## Semantic-token bridge (RAG lexicon → real motion)

30 of the 58 `avatar_sign_lexicon.json` tokens have a confirmed exact bridge to a real motion (full evidence table in `docs/SEMANTIC_BRIDGE.md`). **All 30 are now `ready`**, including the 3 that bridge to Isharah (`INCREMENT`→زياده, `ATTRIBUTE`→صفه, `READ`→قراءه), now that Isharah generation is complete. The other 28 lexicon concepts have no exact match in any dataset and remain unbridged — this is unrelated to physical motion coverage reaching 99.6%: a token can only bridge if the lexicon's own token name or a human-curated alias exactly matches a dataset label, and 28 CS-education concepts simply have no corresponding sign recorded in any of the three datasets under an exact label. Generating (or fully covering) the physical motion library does not, and must not, invent new semantic bridges — see `backend/tests/test_motion_contract.py::test_full_dataset_generation_does_not_invent_semantic_bridges`.

This bridge table lives in `backend/app/motions/manifest.py::LEXICON_TOKEN_BRIDGE` and is the only place such mappings should be added, one verified entry at a time.
